evidence: tcpcl.lisp:635-643 `(fnn-store-indeterminate (e) ... (setq code +fnn-exit-uncertain+)) (fnn-store-error (e) (fnn-err "tcpcl: ~a" e) (setq code +fnn-exit-refused+)) ...` sits inside the fnn-accept-loop handler. io.lisp:77 `(define-condition fnn-store-fault (fnn-store-error) ())`, so every fnn-fault is caught as a refusal. Neither branch leaves the loop (io.lisp:5721-5723 loops until ONCE). The file header says: "a bundle whose staging barrier did not complete is uncertain, its acknowledgement is never released, the session is terminated and the process exits 3." bp.lisp:785-791 shows the intended pattern: re-signal indeterminate and fault.
fix: Re-signal fnn-store-indeterminate and fnn-store-fault out of the accept loop, as bp receive does, and give only plain fnn-store-error the refused code.

reviewer: fnn-tcl-stage (tcpcl.lisp:264-274) turns an fsync/rename os-error into fnn-indeterminate. fnn-tcl-act re-signals it (tcpcl.lisp:396-403), so it leaves fnn-tcl-session. The listen handler (tcpcl.lisp:635-643) catches it, only sets code to 3, and fnn-accept-loop (io.lisp:5721-5723) goes on accepting when ONCE=0. The next session's (setq code (fnn-tcl-exit-code conn)) overwrites that 3, so the process may not exit 3 at all. fnn-store-fault is a subclass of fnn-store-error (io.lisp:77), so faults map to +fnn-exit-refused+. This contradicts the file header (tcpcl.lisp:22-25) and the re-signal pattern in bp.lisp:785-791. Severity is limited because tcpcl listen is the lab/interop verb, not the served node.
scenario: 1) `tcpcl listen PORT 0 ...`: fnn-tcl-stage's fnn-fsync-dir fails (EIO), which raises fnn-indeterminate. The handler sets code 3 and the loop accepts the next peer, which stages and renames more files into the same spool after an ambiguous persistence failure. The process never exits 3. 2) With ONCE=1, an internal fault (for example `TCPCL delivery result did not match held final ACK` or an invalid spool plan) exits with the refused code. A fault looks like an ordinary refusal.
title: tcpcl listen reports a fault as refused and keeps accepting after an uncertain staging barrier
